messages:
Devin: quick heads-up from today's profiler run — seeing ~12% drop in tokens/sec on g5 when tool/function calls + structured outputs are frequent.
Rachael: can you summarize what the trace shows? kernel churn? batch sizes?
Devin: batch fragmentation at the queue boundary. avg batch size fell from ~16 to ~9 when stop-token induced pauses happen. kernel rebinds per request also increased (we bind fallback kernels for structured-output paths). KV cache cold misses went up ~3x.
Mike: immediate_flush_on_stop was a conservative change to avoid waiting forever for tool responses. it helps latency but obviously fragments batches. any measured p99 impact?
Devin: p99 latency is basically stable vs baseline for short prompts, but cost and throughput hit are non-trivial. quick numbers: baseline tokens/sec 10.25k -> 9.02k with immediate flush on our test suite.
sre-oncall: do we have a short config to try softening the behavior? even 10–30ms hold could help.
Devin: tried 20ms hold_window_ms in the queue policy — batch size recovered to ~14 and tokens/sec up ~9% vs immediate-flush case, but p99 increased ~0.7%. kernel rebinds dropped but not gone: structured-output paths still select a different kernel family sporadically.
Rachael: maybe prefer a kernel family (e.g., quant_kv) for the entire decode when structured outputs are likely, instead of switching mid-request. we could add a kernel_hint in the request metadata.
Mike: +1. also consider adaptive policy: default to immediate flush if wait queue depth > N or latency budget low, otherwise hold for the soft window.
Devin: quick experiment config I used:
```
queue_policy:
  hold_window_ms: 20
  stop_flush: softened
kernel_selection:
  static_bias: 0.8
  prefer_kv_family: true
```
Devin: results: tokens/sec 10250 -> 11150 for canary traffic, cost per 1M tokens down ~6%. saw fewer kernel swaps but padding overhead increased when batch shape mismatched.
ci-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout exp-2026-03-17-001 scheduled to 10% g5 cluster.
Rachael: let's add instrumentation for 'toolcall-paused' events in batch traces and a regression alert for kernel-churn spikes + p99 latency + tokens/sec drop.
Mike: agree. doc note: hold_window trades throughput for p99; recommend default 10ms on hosted API and route override for high-throughput routes.
Devin: I'll attach flamegraphs and traces after the canary finishes. immediate next steps: keep hold_window_ms=20 for canary, set static_bias=0.8, add a route-level override and a regression alert.
sre-oncall: if canary stable, roll to 30% tomorrow morning.
Rachael: also add a short test in the perf harness that injects toolcall-induced stop tokens and asserts no >10% throughput regression.
Devin: on it — experiment id exp-2026-03-17-001. will post artifacts in #eng-runtime-perf when ready.
